Implementation Plan

I've written the implementation plan below. The fix extends the existing merged-PR guard and adds no new script or workflow.

**Implementation plan: merged-PR guard trusted a redirected `cd` / `exit` it could not prove ran**

Refs #3576 (the security audit tracker; it carries `ai:security-audit`, so the PR body must use `Refs`, never a closing keyword).

**Planning ref**
- `git rev-parse HEAD`: `a31c945cd5e759081ff40edc5f3fcc6ea55509a5`
- Branch: `ai/issue-5824`, which matches the integration branch metadata (no mismatch).

**Automation and wiring (§20.E)**
- Change type: modifies existing code only. No new script, workflow, scheduler entry or long-running supervisor.
- Entry point: the existing Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`, which runs on every Bash tool call. Its byte-identical twin `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` reaches consumers through the existing `@stable` sync.
- DB work: none.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry: none needed (nothing new is introduced).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `_shell_segments_with_operators` / `_guarded_git_invocations` / `_request_confirmation` in `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`
Scope-mode justification: The finding is one fail-open path. The guard drops redirections when it parses a segment, then assumes a literal `cd` succeeded and a `|| exit` either ran or proves the `cd` succeeded. I tested this in bash: `cd /tmp >/missing/cd || exit >/missing/exit; pwd` prints the original directory and keeps running, because a builtin whose redirection fails does not run at all. The fix stays inside the existing parser and the decision loop.
- It treats a `cd` or `exit` whose redirection could fail as "directory unknown". That reuses the existing uncertain path, which falls back to checking the session checkout.
- It makes an uncertain `git push` ask for confirmation, using the same `ask` mechanism the guard already uses for pushes it cannot verify (CLAUDE.md §21.C).
- Completing this (the confirmation step plus a narrow `/dev/null` allowlist that keeps the common `cd X 2>/dev/null || exit 1` idiom working) costs well under 30 LOC more than the bare redirect check. It adds no dependency or interface, so per the "Boil the Lake" rule it is included. The priority order from §6 applies: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed.

**1. Files likely to change**
- `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: parser, invocation resolver, Bash evaluation loop, module docstring (lines 13–19).
- `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: must stay byte-identical to the file above. `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:1078` enforces this, so copy the file after editing.
- `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`: new regression tests.
- `changelog.d/6289-merge-guard-redirected-cd-exit.md` (new): `<!-- changelog: fixed -->` fragment following CLAUDE.md §20. The issue number 6289 comes from the AI-memory clarify record; if the issue number turns out different, use `<issue>-merge-guard-redirected-cd-exit.md`.

**2. Functions and modules to implement**

a) New `_shell_segments_with_redirects(command) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], bool]]`. The name is confirmed unused.
- Move the current body of `_shell_segments_with_operators` (lines 250–291) here unchanged. Add a per-segment flag, `redirect_may_fail`.
- When a redirect token is seen, remember the operator. When its target token is consumed (the existing `redirect_target` branch), set `redirect_may_fail = True` unless both of these hold:
  - the operator, after the existing fd-prefix stripping, is one of `>`, `>>`, `>|`, `&>`, `&>>`, `<`;
  - the target is exactly `/dev/null`.
- Everything else sets the flag:
  - other file targets;
  - fd duplications (`>&N`, `<&N`, `2>&1`), because an earlier `exec N>&-` in the same command can close the fd;
  - here-docs and here-strings (`<<`, `<<<`);
  - `<>`;
  - a redirect with no target before a separator or end of input.
- Reset the flag whenever a segment is emitted.

b) `_shell_segments_with_operators` becomes a thin wrapper: `[(op, tokens) for op, tokens, _ in _shell_segments_with_redirects(command)]`. Its return shape is unchanged, because it is pinned by `test_fd_prefix_only_removed_for_supported_redirects` and used by the unparseable-command check at line 1300 (§10).

c) `_guarded_git_invocations` (lines 328–414) iterates `_shell_segments_with_redirects`.
- `|| exit` skip (line 337): add `and not redirect_may_fail`. A redirected `exit` then falls through to the existing rule `operator not in ("", "&&", ";", "\n")`, which sets `working_directory = None`. The next `git` is marked uncertain and checked against the session checkout with the existing warning.
- `cd` branch (line 346): if `redirect_may_fail`, set `working_directory = None`. Keep the existing `conditional_cd` update and `continue`.
- Add a short comment at both sites citing this finding: a builtin whose redirection fails does not run, so neither "cd succeeded" nor "exit ran" may be inferred from the text.

d) `_evaluate_bash` (lines 1279–1392), to fail closed for pushes:
- Add a list, `uncertain_push_reasons` (the name is confirmed unused).
- For each invocation with `invocation.subcommand == "push" and invocation.warning`, append the warning before the target loop. That way a later `continue` for a detached HEAD, missing slug or default branch cannot skip it.
- At the end, if there are no `blocks`, issue one `_request_confirmation` covering both lists:
  - uncertain-push text, for example: "could not determine the directory `git push` runs in (shell control flow or redirection); checked the session checkout instead";
  - the existing bulk-push text.
- Bulk-only output keeps its exact current wording, so the bulk path stays backward compatible.
- `git commit` with an uncertain directory keeps today's warn-and-check-checkout behaviour, matching §21.C: a local commit strands nothing until it is pushed.

e) Module docstring: state that a `cd` or `exit` carrying a redirect that could fail (anything except a plain `/dev/null` target) is treated as unresolvable, and that a push in an unresolvable directory asks for confirmation after the checkout check.

**3. Data structures affected**
- An internal per-segment tuple gains a bool, through the new helper only.
- `_GitInvocation` and `_GuardTarget` are unchanged.
- No persisted state, cache format, env var or log key changes.

**4. API or interface changes**
- Hook protocol output: a push whose effective directory cannot be resolved, and that the checkout check did not block, now emits a `permissionDecision: ask` JSON line where before it only emitted a warning.
- Exit codes are unchanged (0 or 2).
- `CLAUDE_PR_MERGE_GUARD=off` still disables the merged-PR check.

## Decisions

### D1 — Treat a redirected `cd` / `exit` as unknown, not as executed
- Chosen: mark the effective directory unknown (`None`) whenever a `cd` or `|| exit` segment carries a redirect that could fail. Reuse the existing uncertain path, which checks the session checkout and warns.
- Alternatives considered:
  - Try to predict whether a redirect target is writable by stat-ing the path. Rejected: it is racy and spoofable, and stat-ing parent directories still cannot decide fd duplications.
  - Reject every redirected `cd` / `exit` outright. Rejected: it blocks harmless idioms.
- Why: the guard must never execute shell text, and it cannot prove a redirect will succeed. Unknown is the only sound answer (fail closed, §6 Security first).

### D2 — Allowlist only literal `/dev/null` file redirects
- Chosen: `>`, `>>`, `>|`, `&>`, `&>>` and `<` to exactly `/dev/null` (with an optional numeric fd prefix) keep the directory resolvable. Everything else, including `2>&1`, makes it unknown.
- Alternatives considered:
  - No allowlist. Rejected: `cd "$dir" 2>/dev/null || exit 1` is a common idiom and would start prompting.
  - Also allow fd duplications. Rejected: `exec 2>&-` earlier in the same command can make `2>&1` fail.
- Why: opening `/dev/null` cannot fail without root changes to the device node, so this keeps today's behaviour for the common case with no added exposure.

### D3 — An uncertain push asks; an uncertain commit warns
- Chosen: after the session-checkout check, collect uncertain-directory pushes and issue one `ask` confirmation unless something already blocked.
- Alternatives considered:
  - Hard-block every uncertain push (exit 2). Rejected: it is disruptive, and the guard elsewhere asks rather than blocks when it cannot verify (§21.C).
  - Keep warning only. Rejected: the session checkout may not be where the push runs (for example `cd A; cd B >x || exit; git push` runs in `A`), so the warning alone fails open.
- Why: this matches the finding's recommendation ("fail closed for pushes when shell control flow or the effective directory cannot be determined") and reuses the existing confirmation mechanism.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: the Bash command text written by the model is untrusted input to a permission hook. The hook must derive authorization only from what it can prove statically. It never executes the text and never treats unproven control flow as success.
- Authorization: this surface is the merged-PR push/commit guard (CLAUDE.md §21). No new endpoint or surface is added. The API-write confirmation path (`_api_write_requires_confirmation`) is untouched.
- Input validation: redirect operators and targets are compared exactly (string equality with `/dev/null`, a fixed operator set). Nothing is expanded or resolved from the command text.
- Abuse cases covered:
  - The finding's own command: `cd <non-repo dir> >/missing/cd || exit >/missing/exit; git push origin`.
  - `cd <other repo> >/missing; git push`.
  - `cd A; cd B 2>&1 || exit; git push`, where the push runs in `A` and not the checkou
